question.problem:
$$
B=\{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -2\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\},\,C=\{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4\end{aligned}]\},\,[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ -9\end{aligned}].
$$

 

The bases $B$ and $C$ of ${R}^{2}$ and the coordinates of the vector $x$ relative to the basis $B$ are given above. Find $[x]_{C}.$

current_example.problem:
The bases $\mathcal{B}$ and $\mathcal{C}$ of $\mathbb{R}^2$ and the coordinates of the vector $\mathbf{x}$ relative to the basis $\mathcal{B}$ are given below. Find $[\mathbf{x}]_{\mathcal{C}}.$ 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14275167/assets/2f76ac469314a3c09ec3b95157485fde7ea31e208eb336b3b47a177d92084508.svg)
current_example.worked_solution:
Let's denote the vectors of $\mathcal{B}$ and $\mathcal{C}$ as $\{ \mathbf{b}_1,\mathbf{b}_2 \}$ and $\{ \mathbf{c}_1,\mathbf{c}_2 \},$ respectively.

The change-of-coordinates matrix from $\mathcal{B}$ to $\mathcal{C}$ is a matrix whose columns are the vectors of $\mathcal{B}$ relative to the basis $\mathcal{C}.$

So, we need to find the coordinates of $\mathbf{b}_1$ and $\mathbf{b}_2$ relative to the basis $\mathcal{C}.$ We can do this simultaneously by considering the matrix
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14275167/assets/7bc48363280598a9b1bf2713d34582d43b79fbbd24a2f908a02a2121547274b8.svg)

Reducing the left-hand side to reduced row-echelon form using Gaussian elimination, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 1 & 1 \\ 6 & 13 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-6){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -5 & -7\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-2){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 11 & 15 \\ 0 & 1 & -5 & -7\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the change-of-coordinates matrix $P_{\small\mathcal{B}\to\mathcal{C}}$ is
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14275167/assets/7d178556c3059e5a4251842ca5ce70ba0007d6a59677c77d947948901500a5c2.svg)

Finally, we compute $[\,\mathbf{x}\,]_{\mathcal{C}}\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}[\,x\,]_{C} & ={P}_{B\to C}[\,x\,]_{B} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}11 & 15 \\ -5 & -7\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-7 \\ 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
